questions.question: Calculate both liquidity ratios for Zanele's Trading and give a two-sided interpretation of the results.
questions.expected_answer: Current ratio: current assets R44 400 (inventories 11 100 + receivables 8 100 + cash 25 200) to current liabilities R11 100 — exactly 4:1. Acid test: (44 400 − 11 100) = R33 300 to R11 100 — 3:1, testing payment ability even if no stock sells. Both sit well above the guideline norms of roughly 2:1 and 1:1 — safe, but the mature comment runs both ways: excess liquidity means idle resources — R24 500 dozing in the bank is not earning the 50% mark-up or settling the 10% loan. Too low endangers the bills; too high spends opportunity.

questions.question: Calculate the solvency ratio and distinguish solvency from liquidity, giving a scenario for each mismatch.
questions.expected_answer: Solvency: total assets R55 600 to total liabilities R27 600 (loan 16 500 + payables 11 100) — about 2:1, comfortably above the 1:1 boundary below which a business is insolvent. Liquidity is the short game (current items only — this year's bills against this year's resources); solvency is the whole game (everything against everything). Mismatches: solvent but illiquid — heavy with equipment yet unable to find Friday's wages; liquid but sinking — cash in the till while total debts outgrow total assets. Solvency also anchors going concern: carrying assets at useful values presumes a future.

questions.question: Calculate return on owner's equity and give the owner risk-weighed advice.
questions.expected_answer: Average equity: (22 000 + 28 000)/2 = R25 000. Return: 10 500/25 000 × 100 = 42%. Against a safe fixed deposit at about 7%, the business returned six times the safe rate — on the numbers, emphatically worth it. The complete answer weighs risk: the deposit's rate is promised while the business's return was earned through labour and risk and may not repeat, so a business should beat the safe rate comfortably — the excess is the wage of risk. A return barely above the bank's would mean the owner works and carries risk for almost nothing extra: rethink.
